outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the programme has moved on several fronts: the global Fourier-Jacobi case for unitary groups was posted as a three-part proof (April 2024 v1; the parts completing it in January 2026, which I could not find refereed or checked by anyone outside the authors), non-tempered cases for general linear groups were claimed settled over archimedean fields (Chen-Chen July 2025 with Boisseau November 2025, the second half of the combination unlocated), a real tempered Fourier-Jacobi metaplectic case was posted (January 2026), and several global non-tempered families were posted (Haan-Kwon, May 2026). No event I found settles the local conjecture for all classical families over real and p-adic fields, and no AI system is named in any event.
problem_asks: The bullet reads: 'Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture: a restriction problem in representation theory of real or p-adic Lie groups.' Unpacked from the statement alone: (1) LOCAL, over a real field R or a p-adic field F: for the classical restriction pairs (SO(n+1),SO(n)), (U(n+1),U(n)), the symplectic-metaplectic pairs (Mp(2n) x Sp(2m) or Sp x Mp), and GL(n+1) x GL(n) as the GGP pairs, for irreducible representations pi of the larger group and sigma of the smaller group the bullet asks about restriction, i.e. the multiplicity dim Hom_H(pi (x) sigma, C). (2) Multiplicity one: that this dimension is at most one for the relevant pairs. (3) The criterion: which pairs (pi, sigma) have nonzero Hom, described in terms of Langlands or Arthur parameters and local root numbers, including the refined statement that picks out the unique member of an L-packet with multiplicity one. (4) Coverage: all classical families in the programme (Wikipedia says the conjecture 'has slightly different forms for the different classical groups'), tempered and non-tempered (Arthur-type) representations, and generic and non-generic representations, over both real and p-adic fields. (5) NOT stated in the bullet: the global (automorphic period versus central L-value) statements and the Ichino-Ikeda refinement. These belong to the same programme and are recorded below as neighbouring events. Whether they bear on the bullet is left to the judging pass.

events.what_happened: Chan and Savin, 'A vanishing Ext-branching theorem for (GL_{n+1}(F), GL_n(F))', arXiv 1803.09131 (March 2018), published Duke Math. J. 170(10) (2021). Proves Prasad's Ext-vanishing conjecture for generic pairs over p-adic F. Predates the window.
events.revisions: Journal version Duke Math. J. 170(10), 15 July 2021 (per search snippet).
events.delivers: Ext^i_H(pi, sigma) = 0 for i >= 1 when pi and sigma are generic irreducible representations of GL_{n+1}(F) and GL_n(F), F p-adic. This is an Ext-level analogue of the multiplicity statement, not the multiplicity-one or nonvanishing criterion itself.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks outside the generic GL case: the Hom criterion for non-generic and non-tempered pairs, all orthogonal, unitary and symplectic pairs, and archimedean fields.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in volume 170, issue 10 (2021), per search snippet

events.direction: Confirms the Ext-level version of Prasad's prediction for generic pairs. It does not cut against the conjecture and is not a multiplicity or criterion result.

events.what_happened: Gurevich, 'On restriction of unitarizable representations of general linear groups and the non-generic local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture', arXiv 1808.02640 (August 2018). Proves one direction of the GL_{n+1} x GL_n prediction for unitarizable representations. Settles the full conjecture when one representation in the pair is generic (per search snippets). Journal reference reported in a snippet as J. Eur. Math. Soc. 2022, not verified on the journal page. Predates the window. Its Theorem 5.7 is corrected in an appendix posted December 2025 (see the pattanayak-2025-12 event).
events.revisions: Journal reference J. Eur. Math. Soc. 2022 (from snippets, unverified). Theorem 5.7 correction appended in arXiv 2512.11696 (Dec 2025).
events.delivers: Restricted to GL_{n+1}(F) x GL_n(F) over a p-adic field: one direction of the non-generic prediction for unitarizable representations, and the full prediction when either representation of the pair is generic. Not the archimedean case, not the classical families.
events.remains: The converse direction for non-generic pairs in the unitarizable class, and all non-GL cases. Theorem 5.7 as stated has been shown insufficient (see the correction event).
events.doubts: Theorem 5.7 was shown in December 2025 not to be correct as stated; the author of the paper wrote an appendix correcting it. The author states the error does not affect the other results of the paper (per the arXiv 2512.11696 abstract and appendix as summarised in search snippets; the rest of the appendix was not read by me).

withdrawn.what: Theorem 5.7's necessary conditions are insufficient; a counterexample is given in Appendix A of arXiv 2512.11696, written by the same author (Maxim Gurevich). The paper's other results are stated to be logically independent of Theorem 5.7.

events.direction: Confirms the GL_n prediction in the cases it covers. The correction narrows one stated criterion but does not contradict the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Cheng Chen, 'The local Gross-Prasad conjecture over Archimedean local fields', arXiv 2102.11404: v1 22 Feb 2021, latest v6 15 Jan 2025. Published Pacific J. Math. 339 (2025), received 25 Nov 2022, accepted 25 Aug 2025, published 1 Sep 2025. The PJM abstract says it proves the local GP conjecture over R and C 'based on the tempered cases of Luo and the author'. The arXiv v6 abstract says it 'completes the proof for the generic cases of the local Gross-Prasad conjecture'. Predates the window (first posting 2021). Its in-window revisions are v6 (Jan 2025) and the journal version (Sep 2025).
events.revisions: v1 22 Feb 2021; v2 17 Mar 2021; v3 17 Apr 2021; v4 23 Nov 2022; v5 26 Jan 2023; v6 15 Jan 2025 (latest). Pacific J. Math. 339 (2025) 133-166, published 1 Sep 2025.
events.delivers: Local GGP over R and C: the arXiv v6 abstract says the generic cases are completed; the PJM abstract says the result is proved over R and C on the basis of Luo's and Chen-Luo's tempered cases. The two descriptions differ on whether the tempered cases are in scope (see disputes). Either way, this is the archimedean local multiplicity-and-criterion statement for SO and related pairs, following Mœglin-Waldspurger.
events.remains: Per the arXiv v6 wording, non-generic (non-tempered) archimedean cases if only generic is proven. Per the PJM wording, the full archimedean statement depends on tempered inputs from Luo and Chen-Luo. Unitary and symplectic-metaplectic archimedean pairs are not covered by this paper.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted 25 Aug 2025 and published 1 Sep 2025, per the MSP journal page

events.doubts: The arXiv v6 abstract and the PJM abstract describe the scope differently: 'generic cases' in arXiv v6 against 'based on the tempered cases of Luo and the author' in PJM. A 2025 Paris talk abstract (per search snippet) is reported as describing the field as having reached a complete proof 'in all cases'. That is a talk abstract, not a write-up, and I could not read it. I did not identify any published rebuttal.
events.direction: Confirms the archimedean local GGP prediction in the cases the paper covers. It does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Chen and Luo, 'Bessel models for real unitary groups: the tempered case', Duke Math. J. 172(5) (2023), per a search snippet. Cited as [CL22] in arXiv 2601.09062 and in arXiv 2102.11404. Proves the local GGP for tempered L-packets of real unitary groups in the Bessel case, by theta lifts. The arXiv posting date was not located. The year 2022 is taken from the citation label and is not verified.
events.delivers: Local GGP for tempered L-packets of real unitary groups in the Bessel model case. Not the Fourier-Jacobi case, not non-tempered representations, not p-adic fields.
events.remains: Non-tempered real unitary cases; the Fourier-Jacobi real unitary case (separately, see the 'real unitary groups' search snippet); all symplectic-metaplectic cases over R.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published as volume 172, issue 5 (2023), per search snippet
checked_by.where: Citation only: Duke Math. J. 172(5) (2023), per search snippet; no URL opened

events.doubts: A search snippet attributes the tempered real unitary Bessel case to Hang Xue as well as to Chen and Luo. The authorship of the tempered real unitary result is therefore not settled by what I read. I did not open the Duke paper.
events.direction: Confirms the Bessel-model local prediction for tempered real unitary groups.

events.what_happened: Furusawa and Morimoto, 'On the Gross-Prasad conjecture with its refinement for (SO(5), SO(2)) and the generalized Böcherer conjecture', arXiv 2205.09503 (first submitted 19 May 2022, revised 5 Apr 2024), published Compositio Math. 160(9) (13 Sept 2024) per search snippet. Proves an Ichino-Ikeda-type formula for tempered irreducible cuspidal automorphic representations, using several theta correspondences. Predates the window; the journal publication is in the window.
events.revisions: v1 19 May 2022; v2 5 Apr 2024. Compositio Math. 160(9):2115-2202, published 13 Sept 2024 (per snippet).
events.delivers: Global (automorphic) refinement for the (SO(5), SO(2)) Bessel pair, for tempered cuspidal automorphic representations. A corollary is a generalized Böcherer formula for degree-two Siegel cusp forms. Global, and only the SO(5) x SO(2) pair.
events.remains: The local statement for this pair; the global case for non-tempered representations and for other SO(2n+1) x SO(2) pairs.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published as Compositio Math. 160(9), 2024 (per search snippet)

events.direction: Confirms the global refined prediction for the tempered (SO(5), SO(2)) case.

events.what_happened: Haan, 'Fourier-Jacobi periods and the non-tempered Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for Mp(2n) x Sp(2m)', arXiv 2201.03270. v1 10 Jan 2022 (predates the window). v2 9 Apr 2024 (in the window). v3 30 Jul 2026 (in the window). The v2 abstract says: 'we establish one direction of the tempered GGP conjecture for these pairs in arbitrary coranks'; 'we establish one direction of the non-tempered global GGP conjecture for the symplectic-metaplectic pairs'; and, for a residual packet, 'this packet lies entirely in the residual spectrum or entirely in the cuspidal spectrum'. The ar5iv rendering of v1 has a different first abstract sentence about the non-vanishing of central values of quadratic twists.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jan 2022; v2 9 Apr 2024; v3 30 Jul 2026 (per abs page). Abstract text differs between v1 and v2.
events.delivers: One direction only, for the symplectic-metaplectic pairs (Mp x Sp) in arbitrary corank: the tempered GGP (v2 abstract: 'one direction of the tempered GGP conjecture for these pairs in arbitrary coranks'), and a non-tempered global direction for these pairs (v2 abstract). Which direction is proved is stated in the abstract only; I did not read the body.
events.remains: The converse directions for these pairs; the full tempered and non-tempered statements; the real and p-adic metaplectic cases beyond what is stated.
events.time_since_posted: about 4.7 years (first posting 2022-01; no journal publication found)
events.doubts: Only one direction is claimed. The v1 and v2 abstracts describe the scope differently. No journal publication or external check was found.
events.direction: Confirms one predicted direction for the metaplectic cases. It does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Beuzart-Plessis, Liu, Zhang and Zhu, 'Isolation of cuspidal spectrum, with application to the Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture', arXiv 1912.07169 (December 2019), Annals of Math. 194 (2021). Completes the global GGP and Ichino-Ikeda conjectures for U(n) x U(n+1) in the stable case (per search snippet). Predates the window.
events.revisions: Annals of Math. 194(2) (2021).
events.delivers: Global (automorphic), unitary, stable case: GGP and Ichino-Ikeda for U(n) x U(n+1).
events.remains: The endoscopic global unitary cases (see bpcz-2020-07); the local side; all other classical families.
events.direction: Confirms the global unitary stable-case prediction.

events.what_happened: Beuzart-Plessis, Chaudouard and Zydor, 'The global Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for unitary groups: the endoscopic case', arXiv 2007.05601 (July 2020), Publ. Math. IHES 135 (2022), published online 27 Jan 2022 (per search snippet). Proves the global GGP and Ichino-Ikeda conjectures for U_n x U_{n+1} in all endoscopic cases. Predates the window.
events.revisions: Publ. Math. IHES 135 (2022), 183-336 (per snippet). The arXiv abstract's term '*-generic' changed to '*-regular' in the journal version (per snippet).
events.delivers: Global (automorphic), unitary, endoscopic cases of U_n x U_{n+1}.
events.remains: Global Eisenstein-series and Bessel-period extensions (see bpc-eisenstein-2023-02); local side; other classical families.
events.direction: Confirms the global unitary endoscopic-case prediction.

events.what_happened: Hongyu He, 'On the Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for U(p,q)', arXiv 1508.02032 (August 2015), Inventiones Math. (2017) per search snippet. Proves the GGP conjecture for discrete series representations of U(p,q). Predates the window.
events.revisions: Inventiones Mathematicae 2017 (per snippet).
events.delivers: Local, real, U(p,q): GGP for discrete series representations.
events.remains: Non-discrete-series representations for U(p,q), p-adic and other classical families (partly covered elsewhere, not by this paper).
events.direction: Confirms the real unitary discrete-series prediction.

events.what_happened: Gan and Ichino, 'The Gross-Prasad conjecture and local theta correspondence', arXiv 1409.6824 (September 2014), Inventiones Math. (2016) per search snippet. Proves the Fourier-Jacobi case of the local GP for unitary groups via theta correspondence and Arthur's multiplicity formula. Predates the window.
events.revisions: Inventiones Math. 2016 (per snippet).
events.delivers: Local unitary, Fourier-Jacobi case (the other pairing being the Bessel case).
events.remains: Non-tempered and symplectic-metaplectic cases.
events.direction: Confirms the local Fourier-Jacobi prediction for unitary groups.

events.what_happened: Atobe, 'The local theta correspondence and the local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for the symplectic-metaplectic case', arXiv 1502.03528 (February 2015). Proves the local symplectic-metaplectic GGP over p-adic fields under some assumptions (per search snippets, which describe it as the last local case not established at the time). Predates the window.
events.revisions: A later version exists (arXiv v3 listed in search results). Journal publication not verified.
events.delivers: Local symplectic-metaplectic, p-adic, under unstated-here assumptions (per snippet, 'under some assumptions').
events.remains: The assumptions; the archimedean case; the non-tempered cases.
events.doubts: The 'under some assumptions' qualification is from a search snippet; I did not open the paper and so cannot name the assumptions.
events.direction: Confirms the prediction for the symplectic-metaplectic case under the assumptions.

events.what_happened: Beuzart-Plessis and Chaudouard, 'The global Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for unitary groups II: from Eisenstein series to Bessel periods', arXiv 2302.12331 (February 2023). Published Forum of Mathematics, Pi, online 13 May 2025 (per snippet). Extends the global GGP and Ichino-Ikeda conjectures to certain Eisenstein series on unitary groups, and derives the global Bessel-period case for unitary groups. Predates the window; the journal publication is in the window.
events.revisions: Forum Math. Pi, online 13 May 2025 (per Cambridge snippet); journal listing 'Jan 2025' in another snippet.
events.delivers: Global unitary: an extension to Eisenstein series of the global GGP and Ichino-Ikeda conjectures; application to global Bessel periods of unitary groups.
events.remains: Local side; global Fourier-Jacobi unitary (see blx-2026-01); other classical families.
events.direction: Confirms the global unitary prediction in the Eisenstein and Bessel cases.

events.what_happened: Chan, 'Restriction for general linear groups: the local non-tempered Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture (non-Archimedean case)', arXiv 2006.02623 (June 2020), published Crelle 2022 (per snippet). Proves the local non-tempered GGP prediction for GL_{n+1} x GL_n over p-adic fields, giving a necessary and sufficient criterion for nonzero Hom. Predates the window.
events.revisions: Crelle 2022 (per snippet). arXiv v2 exists.
events.delivers: Local, p-adic, GL_{n+1} x GL_n, non-tempered (Arthur-type and general) representations: the criterion for nonzero Hom.
events.remains: Archimedean GL_n (see chen-chen-2025-07 and boisseau-2025-11); classical non-GL families; the homological (Ext) version.

checked_by.who: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle), refereed

events.direction: Confirms the p-adic GL_n non-tempered prediction; it is the source of the 'relevance' criterion used later.

events.what_happened: Rui Chen, 'Ext-analogues of Gan-Gross-Prasad models vanish for tempered representations', arXiv 2303.12619 (March 2023). Proves Prasad's conjecture that the Ext-analogues of GGP models vanish for tempered representations, over p-adic fields for orthogonal and unitary groups, and derives a conjectural Euler-Poincaré formula. Predates the window.
events.revisions: arXiv v3 exists (per the ar5iv listing).
events.delivers: Ext-analogue vanishing for tempered representations of orthogonal and unitary groups over p-adic fields. This is an Ext-level statement, not the multiplicity-one or criterion statement.
events.remains: Ext vanishing beyond the tempered case; the multiplicity-level statement that would follow from the Euler characteristic formula.
events.direction: Confirms an Ext-level analogue of the GGP model vanishing for tempered cases. It is a different question from the bullet's multiplicity statement and so counts as an analogue.

events.what_happened: Waldspurger's series on the local GGP for special orthogonal groups (tempered case), first on arXiv in 2009 (arXiv 0911.4568, per search snippet), with four publications 2010-2012 (per Wikipedia's status section, as paraphrased). With Mœglin-Waldspurger (2012, generic non-tempered case), this gives the p-adic SO case. Predates the window.
events.revisions: Four papers 2010-2012 (per Wikipedia paraphrase). Not individually opened.
events.delivers: p-adic special orthogonal groups: the tempered local GGP (Waldspurger); the generic non-tempered local GGP (Mœglin-Waldspurger 2012, per Wikipedia paraphrase).
events.remains: The archimedean SO case (see chen-archimedean-2021-02); non-generic non-tempered SO cases; unitary and symplectic-metaplectic p-adic cases beyond the above.
events.doubts: Not individually opened; the dating is from a search snippet and the Wikipedia paraphrase, not from the papers.
events.direction: Confirms the p-adic SO local prediction in the tempered and generic non-tempered cases.

events.what_happened: Zhilin Luo, 'A local trace formula for the local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for special orthogonal groups', arXiv 2009.13947 (September 2020, by arXiv ID). Gives the tempered-part proof for special orthogonal groups over local fields of characteristic zero, combining Waldspurger and Beuzart-Plessis (per snippet). Predates the window.
events.revisions: Not checked.
events.delivers: Local SO case over char-0 local fields: the tempered part.
events.remains: The non-tempered part for SO; the archimedean generic and non-generic parts (see chen-archimedean-2021-02).
events.doubts: Dated by arXiv identifier. Not opened; the tempered-part claim is from a search snippet.
events.direction: Confirms the tempered SO prediction.

events.what_happened: Mohammed Saad Qadri, 'Non-tempered Ext branching laws for the p-adic general linear group', arXiv 2402.07423 (first submitted 12 February 2024; v2 3 December 2024, 'to appear in IMRN' per author comment). Proves an Ext analogue of the local non-tempered GGP for GL_n over p-adic fields when the representations are products of discrete series and their Aubert-Zelevinsky duals (Arthur type).
events.revisions: v1 12 Feb 2024; v2 3 Dec 2024 ('Revised version; to appear in IMRN').
events.delivers: Ext-level analogue (not multiplicity) of the local non-tempered GGP for GL_n, for the Arthur-type class of products of discrete series and their AZ duals, over p-adic fields.
events.remains: The multiplicity statement itself for this class; the Ext analogue beyond this class; classical families; archimedean fields.

checked_by.who: IMRN (accepted per the author's v2 comment, not verified on the journal site)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal, if the comment is accurate
checked_by.what_they_did: Author states it is to appear in IMRN

events.direction: Confirms an Ext-level analogue of the non-tempered GL_n prediction for one class. It is an analogue of the bullet's statement, not the multiplicity statement itself.

events.what_happened: Hongyu He, 'Projection of elliptic orbits and branching laws', arXiv 2401.14984, first submitted 26 January 2024 (the freeze date), v2 18 July 2025. Expository: uses the orbit method and the GGP branching law for (U(p,q), U(p,q-1)) as the main example. Abstract does not claim a new result on GGP.
events.revisions: v1 26 Jan 2024; v2 18 Jul 2025 (current).
events.delivers: Nothing new on the GGP conjecture; it re-expresses the known U(p,q) branching law through projection of coadjoint orbits.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks.
events.direction: No direction: expository. It is recorded because it is dated to the freeze date and mentions GGP.

events.what_happened: Boisseau, Lu and Xue, 'The global Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for Fourier-Jacobi periods on unitary groups', arXiv 2404.07342, v1 posted 10 April 2024. The v2 abstract (30 October 2024) says: 'We prove the Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for Fourier-Jacobi periods on unitary groups and an Ichino-Ikeda type refinement.' It says the strategy compares relative trace formulae in Liu's formulation and 'We develop the full coarse spectral and geometric expansions'. The v3 (6 January 2026), now titled 'Part I: Coarse expansions of the relative trace formulae', says the paper is 'the first of a series of three papers'. Talks: September 2024 (Building Bridges summer school and workshop) and a seminar by Hang Xue on 29 October 2024. These are talks by the authors, not outside checks.
events.revisions: v1 10 Apr 2024; v2 30 Oct 2024 (claims proof); v3 6 Jan 2026 (split; 'first of a series of three'). Parts II and III are separate arXiv papers from 5 Jan 2026 (see blx-2026-01-05).
events.delivers: As claimed in v2: the global GGP conjecture for Fourier-Jacobi periods on unitary groups, with an Ichino-Ikeda type refinement. This is the global automorphic statement for one family of pairs (Fourier-Jacobi model of unitary groups). Not the local statement.
events.remains: Per v3's framing, the proof is completed in the later parts (blx-2026-01-05). Under the bullet's local wording, nothing here; under a global reading, the other families and the local statement.
events.time_since_posted: about 30 months to 11 Oct 2026 (v1 April 2024); no journal publication or outside reading found
events.doubts: The v2 abstract says 'We prove' and the v3 abstract says it is 'the first of a series of three papers' whose complete argument is spread over the series; the claim was split rather than retracted. I found no published external verification, no journal acceptance, and no blog or review engaging with the argument. I did not read the paper past the abstract.
events.direction: Claims to prove the global Fourier-Jacobi unitary case, which confirms the prediction. It does not cut against it.

events.what_happened: Boisseau, Lu and Xue, Parts II and III of the same series, both posted 5 January 2026. Part II (arXiv 2601.01727, 'Comparison of the relative trace formulae'): compares the two relative trace formulae. Part III (arXiv 2601.01738, 'Proof of the main theorems'): computes the spectral expansions of these formulae and states that this 'end[s] the proof of the conjectures via a reduction to the corank zero case'. Part III's comments field says it is 'the third part of a split version of the article at arXiv:2404.07342'.
events.revisions: Part II v1 5 Jan 2026 (single version). Part III v1 5 Jan 2026 (single version). Part I v3 6 Jan 2026.
events.delivers: As the authors state, with Part I, the global GGP for Fourier-Jacobi periods on unitary groups and the Ichino-Ikeda type refinement. Part II only compares the relative trace formulae; Part III carries the spectral part and the corank-zero reduction. Global, one family.
events.remains: Local statement; all other families; any independent check that the three parts together are complete.
events.doubts: The three parts were posted as a split of one article, not as three independent papers, and no outside check exists yet. I did not read the full text of Parts II or III; the claims are from the abstracts. The authors' earlier v2 framing is in blx-2024-04-10.
events.direction: Claims the global Fourier-Jacobi unitary prediction, which confirms it.

events.what_happened: Cheng Chen and Rui Chen, 'Non-tempered Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for Archimedean general linear groups', arXiv 2507.04355 (6 July 2025, single version). Proves the 'period implies relevance' direction of the local non-tempered GGP for GL_{n+1} x GL_n over archimedean fields, using Gourevitch-Sayag-Karshon on annihilator varieties. The abstract says that with a recent result of P. Boisseau on 'relevance implies period', 'this conjecture for general linear groups over Archimedean local fields is settled'.
events.revisions: v1 only (6 July 2025).
events.delivers: One direction (period implies relevance) of the local non-tempered GGP for GL_n over R and C, for Arthur-type pairs. Combined with the converse, claimed to settle the archimedean GL_n non-tempered case.
events.remains: The converse (relevance implies period) unless the Boisseau result is accepted (see boisseau-2025-11 and the citation doubt). Archimedean classical families other than GL_n.
events.doubts: The settlement depends on a 'recent result of P. Boisseau' on relevance implies period. The Boisseau paper I found (arXiv 2511.21798) was posted on 26 November 2025, four months after this paper's July 2025 version, and this paper has no later version. The earlier Boisseau result it cites was not located. Boisseau's 2025 abstract refers to 'previous works of Chan, Chen and Chen', so the combination is acknowledged by its authors.
events.direction: Confirms one direction of the archimedean GL_n non-tempered prediction and, with the converse, claims full settlement for that case. It does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Boisseau, 'Residues of Rankin-Selberg zeta integrals and the split non-tempered Gan-Gross-Prasad conjectures', arXiv 2511.21798 (26 November 2025, single version). Builds a regularisation of the Rankin-Selberg period on GL_n for non-tempered automorphic representations, using residues of zeta integrals. Proves it satisfies the global non-tempered GGP conjecture and its Ichino-Ikeda refinement (the 'relevance implies period' direction, per the paper's abstract and the citing paper). Builds a local version giving a nonzero invariant form on non-tempered representations. The abstract says: 'Combined with previous works of Chan, Chen and Chen, this settles the conjectures over local fields of characteristic zero.'
events.revisions: v1 only (26 November 2025).
events.delivers: Global non-tempered GL_n GGP and Ichino-Ikeda refinement via the residue-regularised period; a local nonzero-form construction. With Chan and Chen-Chen, the author says it settles the non-tempered GL_n conjectures over char-0 local fields.
events.remains: Classical families other than GL_n; the bullet's local statement for these families.
events.doubts: The 'settles' claim is a combination of this paper with Chan (2020) and Chen-Chen (2025), which has not been checked by anyone else. The relation to the 'recent result of P. Boisseau' cited in Chen-Chen (2025) is unresolved (see chen-chen-2025-07).
events.direction: Confirms the relevance-implies-period direction of the global non-tempered GL_n prediction, and claims local settlement in combination. It does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Nhat Hoang Le, 'The local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for GL(V)/U(V)', arXiv 2504.21002 (v1 1 April 2025; v2 4 June 2025; 75 pages). Uses the Waldspurger and Beuzart-Plessis method for Bessel models to study two local relative trace formulae for the twisted GGP, obtains their spectral expansions and a partial geometric comparison. Claims: 'we prove the local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture' for GL(V)/U(V) over nonarchimedean fields, for tempered representations.
events.revisions: v1 1 Apr 2025; v2 4 Jun 2025 ('change template, correct minor typos').
events.delivers: Local, p-adic, tempered, for the twisted GGP pair GL(V)/U(V). The 'twisted' variant is a different pair from the untwisted GGP.
events.remains: The untwisted GGP for this pair (not claimed); non-tempered representations; other classical families; archimedean fields.
events.doubts: Whether a 'twisted' GGP counts as the bullet's problem is a scope question for the judging pass (§2.1). The arXiv note mentions text overlap with an arXiv paper by other authors (1506.01452), which is administrative.
events.direction: Claims the tempered local twisted GGP for GL(V)/U(V). It is a twisted variant and does not directly settle the untwisted pair.

events.what_happened: Nhat Hoang Le, 'The local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for U(V_K)/U(V)', arXiv 2511.01301 (3 November 2025, v1 only). Obtains geometric expansions of a local trace formula and its twisted variant. As an application: 'we prove the local twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for U(V_K)/U(V)' for tempered L-parameters over nonarchimedean fields of odd residual characteristic. Comments field: 'This is a preliminary version. Comments are welcome.'
events.revisions: v1 only (3 Nov 2025).
events.delivers: Local, p-adic, tempered, odd residual characteristic, for the twisted GGP pair U(V_K)/U(V). Twisted variant.
events.remains: Even residual characteristic; non-tempered; the untwisted pair; other families.
events.doubts: Self-described as a preliminary version. Odd residual characteristic is a restriction. Whether the twisted problem counts as the bullet's problem is a scope question for the judging pass.
events.direction: Claims the tempered local twisted GGP for U(V_K)/U(V). A twisted variant, so it does not directly settle the untwisted pair.

events.what_happened: Cheng Chen, Rui Chen and Jialiang Zou, 'Fourier-Jacobi models for real symplectic-metaplectic groups: the basic case', arXiv 2601.09062 (14 January 2026, v1 only). Generalises the Gan-Ichino and Atobe method to R. Proves the basic tempered case of the local GGP for Fourier-Jacobi models of symplectic-metaplectic groups over R, based on the tempered Bessel case of [CL22] (Chen-Luo). A search snippet adds that the main theorem has two parts: multiplicity one for tempered L-parameters, and an epsilon-dichotomy statement (I did not read the theorem in the paper).
events.revisions: v1 only (14 Jan 2026).
events.delivers: Real, symplectic-metaplectic, Fourier-Jacobi, tempered 'basic case'. Multiplicity one and epsilon dichotomy for tempered parameters, per the snippet.
events.remains: Non-tempered real symplectic-metaplectic cases; the non-basic cases; p-adic cases are stated as already known in the introduction (per a snippet, unverified).
events.doubts: Depends on the tempered Bessel result of Chen-Luo, which I could not open. The 'basic case' label is the authors' own restriction.
events.direction: Confirms the basic tempered real Fourier-Jacobi metaplectic prediction. It does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Basudev Pattanayak, 'Quotient branching laws and Gan-Gross-Prasad relevance for general linear groups', arXiv 2512.11696 (v1 12 Dec 2025; v2 3 Aug 2026, comment 'Separated the Q.B.L. of Speh representations'). Proves branching laws for the quotient problem for (GL_{n+1}(F), GL_n(F)) over non-archimedean F for the full class of unitarizable representations, and an explicit algorithm (following Chan) that decides from Zelevinsky or Langlands data whether the relevant Hom space is nonzero. Appendix A, written by Maxim Gurevich, states that the necessary conditions in [Gur, Theorem 5.7] are insufficient, with a counterexample; the appendix says this is logically independent of the other results of [Gur]. Abstract: 'corrects and extends prior work by Gurevich'.
events.revisions: v1 12 Dec 2025; v2 3 Aug 2026 (comment: 'Separated the Q.B.L. of Speh representations').
events.delivers: Non-archimedean GL_{n+1} x GL_n, full unitarizable class: the criterion for the relevant Hom space to be nonzero, made computable. It extends the earlier relevance notion, which covered Arthur-type representations. It does not restate the GL_n multiplicity-one result, which is attributed to Aizenbud-Gourevitch-Rallis-Schiffmann.
events.remains: Archimedean fields; the classical families other than GL_n; the Ext and homological versions.

checked_by.qualification: Author of the paper being corrected, and of the appendix
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote Appendix A correcting Theorem 5.7 of his own 2018 paper (per the arXiv HTML)

events.doubts: The author's affiliation differs between sources: Technion (arXiv HTML) and University of Hong Kong (search snippet). A search snippet credits Rui Chen with the minimal-rank counterexample in the appendix; the arXiv HTML page I read does not show that credit in the text I could see, and I could not read the appendix body (the HTML was truncated and the PDF was not readable as text). I did not read the counterexample.
events.direction: Confirms the GL_n relevance criterion in the full unitarizable class, and identifies an insufficient necessary condition in Gurevich's 2018 Theorem 5.7. The correction does not cut against the conjecture itself.
events.object: Appendix A exhibits a minimal-rank counterexample (per a search snippet, credited to Rui Chen) showing that the stated necessary conditions in [Gur, Theorem 5.7] are not sufficient. I did not read the example itself.

events.what_happened: Haan and Kwon, 'The tower property on the genericity of global theta lifts', arXiv 2410.02625. v1 3 Oct 2024; v2 4 Oct 2024; v3 28 May 2025; v4 11 May 2026, withdrawn. The v1 abstract (as summarised from the page) claims the global GGP conjecture for SO(2n+1) x SO(2), under the assumptions that SO(2) is split and its representation trivial, and says the first occurrence of global theta lifts preserves genericity. The withdrawal notice says the paper 'is significantly outdated and has been superseded by a majorly expanded work with fundamentally new results and a different scope', and points to arXiv 2605.04389.
events.revisions: v1 3 Oct 2024; v2 4 Oct 2024; v3 28 May 2025; v4 11 May 2026 (withdrawn).
events.delivers: As summarised from the abstract page: global GGP for SO(2n+1) x SO(2), with SO(2) split and the representation trivial; Bessel and Fourier-Jacobi periods via L-function analysis.
events.remains: Everything outside those assumptions; the local statement.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the authors as superseded, not for an error. The withdrawal notice does not identify a flaw.

withdrawn.what: Withdrawn version (v4) of arXiv 2410.02625; the authors say it is superseded by arXiv 2605.04389 with 'fundamentally new results and a different scope'.

events.direction: Claims the global SO(2n+1) x SO(2) prediction under split and trivial-character assumptions. It does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Haan and Kwon, 'Special periods and some non-tempered cases of the Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture', arXiv 2605.04389 (v1 6 May 2026; v2 30 July 2026). Abstract: 'we establish a relationship between special periods and special L-values of automorphic representations of classical groups, and prove the non-tempered global Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture in several cases.' Method: Rallis tower property for theta-lift genericity, and Rankin-Selberg analysis. Proves three explicit higher-corank families of non-tempered cases of the global conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 6 May 2026; v2 30 Jul 2026. Replaces arXiv 2410.02625.
events.delivers: Global non-tempered GGP for three explicit higher-corank families of classical groups (families not named in the abstract I read).
events.remains: Local statement; non-tempered cases outside the three families; the remaining cases of the global conjecture.
events.doubts: The three families and the direction of the implication are not stated in the abstract I read. I did not read the paper.
events.direction: Claims three non-tempered global families, which confirms those families of the prediction. It does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Kei Yuen Chan and Mohammed Saad Qadri, 'An inductive Ext non-vanishing theorem for the p-adic general linear group', arXiv 2601.20635 (28 January 2026, v1 only). Proves an embedding theorem for Ext-groups under parabolic induction, and 'a variation of the non-tempered Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture' in the homological branching setting.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Homological (Ext-level) variant of the non-tempered GL_n GGP for p-adic fields. A different question (Ext) from the multiplicity statement.
events.remains: The multiplicity statement itself; classical families; archimedean fields.
events.doubts: Ext-level variant; the abstract does not state an Ext non-vanishing theorem explicitly despite the title.
events.direction: Proves a homological variant of the non-tempered GL_n prediction. An analogue, not the multiplicity statement.

events.what_happened: Pan Yan, 'Uniqueness of Bessel models for GSpin groups', arXiv 2503.20116 (v1 25 March 2025; v2 8 June 2026; Nagoya Math. J. 2026 per the abstract page). Proves uniqueness of general Bessel models for GSpin groups over local fields of characteristic zero, reducing to the spherical case. The abstract page does not mention Gan-Gross-Prasad.
events.delivers: Multiplicity-one for general Bessel models of GSpin groups. A different pair and a different (Bessel-model) question, neighbouring to the GGP programme. Not GGP as stated.
events.remains: The bullet's restriction problem for the classical pairs.

checked_by.what_they_did: Journal reference Nagoya Math. J. 2026 on the abstract page

events.doubts: Recorded as neighbouring work, not GGP. Whether it bears on the bullet is for the judging pass.
events.direction: Multiplicity-one for GSpin Bessel models. It is a different question, neither confirming nor cutting against the bullet.

events.what_happened: Yu Luo, Andreas Mihatsch and Zhiyu Zhang, arithmetic transfer preprint dated 9 September 2025 (per a search snippet, not opened). Proves the arithmetic transfer conjecture of the third author in full generality, and gives new integral models of unitary Shimura varieties at ramified places. It is part of the arithmetic Gan-Gross-Prasad (AGGP) programme.
events.revisions: Not checked.
events.delivers: Arithmetic transfer (one ingredient of the arithmetic GGP / relative trace formula approach). A different question: arithmetic (Chow group and height) rather than the restriction problem of the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet's restriction problem; the full AGGP statement on Chow groups.
events.doubts: Not opened; dated and described from a search snippet. Recorded as a neighbouring event on the arithmetic side.
events.direction: Arithmetic transfer; a different question from the bullet. Neither confirms nor cuts against it.

events.what_happened: Cheng Chen, PhD thesis, University of Minnesota (June 2024), 'A Uniform Approach towards the Local Gan-Gross-Prasad Conjecture' (per a search snippet). The snippet says the thesis notes the proof 'is almost complete', with some cases using a different philosophy, and aims for a uniform proof of all cases generalising Mœglin-Waldspurger.
events.delivers: Local GGP across cases, per the thesis's own claims as summarised by a search snippet. Not read.
events.remains: Unknown: the thesis is not read.
events.doubts: Not opened: the UMN conservancy page returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch. The 'almost complete' wording is from a search snippet.
events.direction: Unknown from what I could read; the thesis claims near-completeness of the local case, which would confirm the prediction if accurate.

disputes.summary: Cheng Chen's archimedean local paper: arXiv v6 (Jan 2025) says it 'completes the proof for the generic cases', while the Pacific J. Math. abstract (published Sept 2025) says the local GP over R and C is proved 'based on the tempered cases of Luo and the author'. A March 2025 IHP talk abstract (search snippet, unread) reports a complete proof 'in all cases'. These are not reconciled in anything I read.

Boisseau, Lu and Xue: the v2 abstract (Oct 2024) says 'We prove the Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for Fourier-Jacobi periods on unitary groups'. The v3 abstract (Jan 2026) says it is 'the first of a series of three papers' and that the complete argument is spread over them. The claim was split rather than withdrawn.

Chen and Chen (arXiv 2507.04355, July 2025) rely on 'a recent result of P. Boisseau' for relevance implies period. The Boisseau paper I found (arXiv 2511.21798) is dated November 2025 and has no earlier version. The earlier result was not located, so the archimedean GL_n settlement claim rests on a citation I could not resolve.

Tempered real unitary Bessel case: Chen-Luo (Duke 2023, cited as [CL22]) in Chen-Chen-Zou and in Chen's archimedean paper, but a search snippet attributes a tempered real unitary local GGP result to Hang Xue. Not reconciled.

Counterexample to Gurevich's Theorem 5.7: the arXiv HTML states that the appendix is written by Maxim Gurevich and that Pattanayak thanks him for it. A search snippet credits Rui Chen with explaining the minimal-rank counterexample. I could not see that credit in the text I read.
Pattanayak's affiliation is given as Technion in the arXiv HTML and as the University of Hong Kong in a search snippet. Not relevant to the mathematics; recorded for the attribution pass.

summary: The bullet is the local GGP restriction problem over R and p-adic fields for all classical families, with multiplicity one, a Hom criterion, and tempered and non-tempered cases. Searches on the name, its variants, the AI angle and the post-2024 literature turned up 32 events, of which 16 are dated in the window (26 January 2024 onward) and 16 predate it. The in-window events are: an Ext-level analogue for GL_n (Qadri, Feb 2024; Chan-Qadri, Jan 2026); an expository GGP example (He, Jan 2024); the Boisseau-Lu-Xue series on global Fourier-Jacobi periods for unitary groups (first posted April 2024, parts II and III in January 2026, each relying on the authors' own account of completion); Chen-Chen (July 2025) and Boisseau (Nov 2025) on non-tempered GL_n over archimedean fields, with a settlement claim that depends on a Boisseau citation I could not locate; Le's two twisted local GGP papers (April and Nov 2025, tempered, twisted); Chen-Chen-Zou (Jan 2026), a basic tempered real Fourier-Jacobi metaplectic case; Pattanayak (Dec 2025), a non-archimedean GL_n relevance criterion that corrects a stated criterion in Gurevich's 2018 Theorem 5.7; and Haan-Kwon (Oct 2024, withdrawn May 2026; and May 2026), global non-tempered families. Chen's archimedean local paper, published in PJM in September 2025, has two conflicting scope descriptions (generic cases in arXiv v6, tempered cases in the journal abstract). No outside reviewer, journal acceptance, or independent check of the 2024 Boisseau-Lu-Xue claim was found, and the three-part 2026 series is unchecked outside its authors. Wikipedia's status section (last edited 23 June 2026, as paraphrased by my fetch) cites results up to 2020 and 2017 and does not mention any event in the window. No AI system is named in any event: about ten searches for AI involvement (lab announcements, Epoch and similar trackers, AI acknowledgements in GGP papers) turned up no GGP result credited to an AI system. Outside GGP, the tracker results include OpenAI and Anthropic model claims on other conjectures (for example an unrelated Szpiro-bound paper and an OpenAI model disproof of the unit-distance conjecture), none about GGP. One snippet reports a Google Gemini disclosure in a single-author 2022 Haan paper; the text of that paper (both arXiv HTML and ar5iv) does not contain it, so I record none_found true with this lead unresolved. Close calls: whether the global unitary Fourier-Jacobi series counts toward the bullet (the bullet's wording is local, so I recorded it as neighbouring but gave the full event record); whether the twisted GGP papers are the same problem; and whether Haan-Kwon's global non-tempered families bear on a bullet that does not state global results. A nearby program is the arithmetic GGP, whose transfer-level result (Luo-Mihatsch-Zhang, Sept 2025) I recorded from a snippet only and did not open.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a substantially advanced record: since 2024 the local-and-global programme has produced several claimed settlements (Chen with Chan and Boisseau for archimedean non-tempered GL_n, the three-part Boisseau-Lu-Xue series for unitary Fourier-Jacobi periods, Le's local twisted tempered cases, Chen-Chen-Zou's real Fourier-Jacobi tempered basic case, and Haan-Kwon's three non-tempered global families), and Chen's thesis describes the local conjecture as almost complete. On that reading the bullet is close to resolved in every family, and only the un-refereed status of the 2024-2026 claims stands between the record and a 'settled' call. Against it: the bullet's own wording is the local statement over real and p-adic fields for every classical family; the settlements cover one family each, or a tempered or generic subset, or a twisted variant; and several key links rest on preprints, withdrawn or superseded versions, or citations I could not resolve.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Refereed publication or an external check of Boisseau-Lu-Xue (2404.07342 v2/v3 and 2601.01727/2601.01738), since their scope and completeness determine the global Fourier-Jacobi unitary case. (2) The earlier 'recent result of P. Boisseau' cited in Chen-Chen (July 2025), to confirm the archimedean GL_n settlement. (3) The published Cheng Chen PJM text, to fix whether the archimedean local result covers tempered cases only or generic cases only. (4) Appendix A of arXiv 2512.11696 read in full, to confirm who found the counterexample and what it shows. (5) The Duke 2023 Chen-Luo paper and its arXiv date, and whether the tempered real unitary Bessel result is Chen-Luo's or Xue's. (6) A survey by Gan, Beuzart-Plessis or another expert stating the current status of the local conjecture for each classical family. (7) For the AI question, the full acknowledgement sections of the 2024-2026 preprints (I read abstracts and partial HTML only).

incomplete: (1) Full texts were not read for most events. For the 2024-2026 preprints I read arXiv abstract pages (and their version history), with partial HTML only for 2201.03270 and 2512.11696. Acknowledgements and contribution statements, which the AI search depends on, were therefore not checked for most events; the none_found values rest on the abstracts and the parts I read. (2) Boisseau-Lu-Xue Parts I-III: abstracts only; the proofs and their completeness are not checked. (3) The Gurevich appendix (arXiv 2512.11696, Appendix A): the counterexample and its exact claim are not read; the PDF was not readable as text, and I did not open the locally saved copy of it, per the project's rule against reading files outside the main directory. (4) Cheng Chen's UMN thesis (June 2024): not read (HTTP 403). (5) Chen-Luo (Duke 2023) and Atobe (2015), Furusawa-Morimoto (2022), BPLZZ (2019), BPCZ (2020), BP-Chaudouard II (2023), Gan-Ichino (2014), He (2015), Chan-Savin (2018), Chan (2020), Rui Chen (2023), Waldspurger (2009) and Luo (2020) were dated from arXiv identifiers or search snippets, and most were not opened; their journal references are from snippets. (6) Several dates are by arXiv identifier (month precision) and are marked as such. (7) The Gemini disclosure lead from a 2022 search snippet (Haan) is unresolved. (8) The earlier Boisseau result cited by Chen-Chen (July 2025) is unresolved. (9) The status of the Wikipedia article was read through a paraphrasing fetch, not verbatim. (10) Non-GGP AI results (e.g. the Szpiro-bound paper, the sphere-packing result, unit-distance disproofs, and the Isaacs-Navarro-Wolf paper) were seen in search results and are not GGP events; they are not recorded as events. (11) Coverage of local GGP for classical families is incomplete: I did not establish the current status of the symplectic-metaplectic p-adic case beyond Atobe's 'under some assumptions', nor the archimedean unitary and symplectic cases beyond Chen-Chen-Zou and Chen. (12) The 2025 Paris talk and the 2025 Chen talk claims (complete proof in all cases) are not recorded as events, because only a snippet was seen.
